chunks: And he also narrated - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from 'Ali from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about breaking the fast of the expiation for an oath, and the expiation for Dhihar, and the expiation for blood [diarrhea/illness]. He said: 'If upon a man is the fasting of two consecutive months, and he breaks his fast or falls ill in the first month, then upon him is to restart the fasting. And if he fasts the first month and fasts some of the second month, then an excuse befalls him, then upon him is only to make up [the missed days].'

These narrations are understood to apply when his illness is one that does not prevent him from fasting, although it causes him some difficulty. Thus, whenever the matter is as we mentioned, it becomes obligatory upon him to restart [the two months], according to what these narrations encompass.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on restarting expiatory fasting if one breaks it due to illness?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad via Abu Basir, highlighting the juristic distinction between absolute impediment and relative difficulty in expiatory fasting. The text clarifies that while severe illness necessitates restarting the two-month sequence, mild hardship only requires making up the missed days, a nuance critical to Shia fiqh regarding kaffarah al-yamin and kaffarah al-dhihar. This ruling underscores the principle that continuity is broken only by genuine inability, not mere inconvenience.
